chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one among you who drinks an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty nights.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the prayer of someone who drinks an intoxicant?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of Samaan ibn Mihran, establishes a specific legal penalty (kaffarah) for consuming khamr, where the individual's prayer is suspended for forty nights. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the spiritual impurity of intoxication, distinguishing it from mere ritual impurity (najis) by affecting the validity of worship rather than just the state of purity. The duration of forty nights is often interpreted as a period of spiritual purification or a specific divine retribution for the loss of divine presence during prayer.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said:’
The one who drinks an intoxication from among you, his Prayer would not be Accepted from him for forty nights’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
If one [of you] drinks intoxicating liquor his Salat (prayer) is not accepted for forty days.’”
